chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام concerning a dead person who died while in janabah: How should he be washed, and how much water suffices for him? He said: He is to be given one ghusl, and that suffices for both janabah and the ghusl of the deceased, because they are two sanctities that have come together in one sanctity.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: The state of major ritual impurity caused by janabah.
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl.
key_terms.حُرْمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ: One single sanctity within which both are combined.
key_terms.غُسْلًا وَاحِدًا: A single ghusl that fulfills the required washing.
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: The ritual washing of the deceased.
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: He is to be ritually washed.

ai.seo_question: If a person dies while in janabah, is one ghusl enough for both janabah and the ghusl of the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a deceased person who died in a state of janabah. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that one ghusl is sufficient for both janabah and the ghusl of the deceased, indicating the legal merging of the two obligations in a single ritual washing.
